name: Bangkok
summary: Start with the old-city temples and cross the river for Wat Arun. Keep shopping and modern-city sights for another day because traffic can turn short distances into long transfers.
seasonNote: Cooler dry-season months are easiest; April is very hot and rainy-season downpours can flood streets.
arrival: Airport Rail Link from Suvarnabhumi connects with the city rail network; Don Mueang has separate rail and bus options.
gettingAround: Mix BTS/MRT with river boats; use metered taxis or app bookings when needed.
cashTip: Carry small baht notes for boats, markets and food; use ATMs thoughtfully because fees can be high.
foodTip: Try boat noodles, pad krapao and mango sticky rice; ask how spicy dishes are and check seafood/pork ingredients.
buyTip: Markets suit textiles and small crafts; avoid expensive gemstones bought under pressure.
baseArea: Siam/Sukhumvit for trains; riverside or old city for temples.

connections.note: Approximate flight time; overnight sleeper rail is a separate slower option.
Check that your flight uses Siem Reap–Angkor airport; road border conditions vary.

items.name: Sorn
items.summary: A three-star celebration of Southern Thai food culture, with rare regional ingredients and fiery, deeply layered cooking.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.

whyVisit: A three-star celebration of Southern Thai food culture, with rare regional ingredients and fiery, deeply layered cooking.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Three MICHELIN Stars (exceptional cuisine), the guide’s highest award.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.
